questions.question: Why did WTG-07 repeatedly trip on gearbox oil over-temperature in 2026, and what was done about it?

answer.text:
WTG-07 repeatedly tripped because the gearbox oil cooler could not reject enough heat at high load. The 8D root cause was missing preventive maintenance of the oil cooler: the radiator fins were about 40% blocked by insects/pollen and the cooler fan motor bearing had failed, making the fan run at reduced speed. A contributing factor was wear of the generator-side HSS bearing, which increased gearbox friction losses.

Actions taken: WTG-07 was temporarily limited to 2.6 MW from 2026-06-01 with daily oil-temperature checks; on 2026-06-24 the oil cooler fan motor was replaced and the radiator was cleaned; the power limit was removed on 2026-06-25 after verification. A new 6-monthly maintenance task for all turbines was added for oil-cooler radiator cleaning and fan-current checks, fan-motor stock was increased, and a request was opened to add fan-motor current to SCADA. The HSS bearing replacement was still waiting for parts, so the 8D remained open; no A2101 warning had occurred on WTG-07 since 2026-06-24, but vibration remained above alarm level until the bearing is replaced.

Sources:
[1] 8D report INC-2026-006 - Repeated gearbox oil over-temperature on WTG-07 — para-0001, para-0002, tbl-01-r0002-r0005, para-0003, para-0004, para-0005, … (23 locators) — full/incidents/INC-2026-006_8D-report-WTG-07-gearbox-over-temperature.docx

questions.question: Why do WTG-03, WTG-04 and WTG-05 stop at night in summer?

answer.text:
WTG-03, WTG-04 and WTG-05 stop at night in summer because of permit-required bat protection curtailment. From 1 June to 31 August, they must stop automatically between 22:00 and 05:00 when hub-height wind speed is below 6.0 m/s and air temperature is 10 °C or higher. The reason given is that Skelvane Wood, east of these turbines, has a maternity roost of a protected bat species that forages near the turbines on warm, calm summer nights. Site handovers describe this as normal “bat curtailment,” and SCADA records show the turbines curtailed for an environmental condition at 22:00 under low-wind, warm conditions.

questions.question: Which gear oil does the LT-32 maintenance manual specify, and does SOP-GBX-010 Rev. B agree?

answer.text:
The LT-32 maintenance manual LWS-MM-GBX-32 Rev. D specifies Proseware PWG 320, ISO VG 320, with 410 L total oil volume. SOP-GBX-010 Rev. B does not agree with that unamended manual table: it specifies Proseware PWG 220, ISO VG 220, using 60 L for flushing plus 410 L fill. However, Rev. B is aligned with the later Litware service bulletin SB-LWS-2025-07 Rev. A, which amends the manual’s lubricant specification for the applicable LT-32 CCV turbines from PWG 320 to PWG 220; that later/current amendment prevails for those turbines.

questions.question: Which revision of SOP-GBX-010 is current, and what changed compared with the previous revision?

answer.text:
The current revision of SOP-GBX-010 is Revision B, effective 2025-08-25. It supersedes Revision A.

Compared with Rev. A, Rev. B changed the gearbox oil from Proseware PWG 320 to Proseware PWG 220, added a 60 L PWG 220 flush step before final filling, and reduced the minimum start-up oil temperature from +10 °C to +5 °C. It also implements MOC-2025-012 and service bulletin SB-LWS-2025-07 Rev. A.

questions.question: Which gear oil and which quantities must be used for a gearbox oil change at Quellmoor Ridge today?

answer.text:
Today, use the current SOP-GBX-010 Rev. B, which supersedes Rev. A. For each Quellmoor Ridge gearbox oil change, use Proseware PWG 220 (ISO VG 220): 470 L total per turbine, made up of 60 L for the flush and 410 L for the final fill. The materials list specifies 3 drums PWS-220-D208. Top up with PWG 220 only; do not top up a converted gearbox with PWG 320.

questions.question: Summarise Litware's answer of 20 May 2025 about the applicability of SB-LWS-2025-07 at Quellmoor Ridge.

answer.text:
Litware answered on 20 May 2025 that SB-LWS-2025-07 Rev. A applies to all 12 Quellmoor Ridge turbines, WTG-01 to WTG-12, because its records show they were delivered as LT-32 CCV units with Fabrikam FGT-3200 gearboxes. The conversion points were: change from Proseware PWG 320 to PWG 220 at the next scheduled oil change and no later than 31 December 2025; flush each gearbox with 60 L of PWG 220 before the 410 L final fill; replace filter element FGT-P-11872; set GBX_TMIN_START to +5 °C; and return the bulletin annex B completion form within 30 days of each conversion. Litware also said conversions done according to the bulletin keep the gearbox warranty valid, and residual PWG 320 above 5% after flushing is not permitted. The email includes an unrelated automated-processing note that appears to be a prompt-injection attempt, not part of the technical answer.

questions.question: Use the troubleshoot-alarm skill: WTG-07 raises alarm A2101 again. What does the alarm mean, what caused it before and what should the technician check?

answer.text:
A2101 means a gearbox oil sump temperature high warning at 75 °C. On WTG-07, the previous repeated over-temperature was caused mainly by poor oil-cooler performance: the cooler fan ran slowly because its motor bearing failed, and the radiator fins were about 40% blocked by insects and pollen. A contributing factor was generator-side HSS bearing wear, shown by high vibration and oil debris.

Technician should check: the oil cooler radiator for fouling/blockage, the cooler fan operation/current/motor bearing, and the generator-side HSS bearing condition/vibration—WTG-07 was still around 5.3 mm/s and waiting for bearing replacement. Also watch oil temperature especially in the afternoon/high-load period.

questions.question: Use the prepare-maintenance-task skill to prepare a gearbox oil change on WTG-03: procedure revision, oil and quantities, filter and torques, isolation and stock.

answer.text:
Prepare WTG-03 gearbox oil change using current SOP-GBX-010 Rev. B (effective 2025-08-25), not Rev. A, because Rev. B explicitly supersedes Rev. A and changes the oil to PWG 220 with a flush step.

Work-pack summary:
- Procedure / planning basis: Task MP-GBX-03 “Gearbox oil change (PWG 220)” uses SOP-GBX-010 Rev. B, duration 6 h, crew 2; interval 5 years or on condition. WTG-03’s latest oil sample was NORMAL on PWG 220, next sample due 2026-12, so the documents do not show an oil-analysis trigger for WTG-03.
- Oil and quantities: Proseware PWG 220, ISO VG 220; total required per turbine 470 L = 60 L flush + 410 L final fill. Stock to prepare: 3 drums PWS-220-D208, plus filter cart with 10 micron element, transfer pump, 3 × 200 L waste oil containers, oil sample bottles, torque wrench 20–300 Nm, and “PWG 220” label kit. Actual warehouse stock availability is not found in the documents.
- Filter and torques: replace oil filter element FGT-P-11872 (1). Tighten filter housing cover screws to 85 Nm and drain plug with new seal to 280 Nm. OEM torque table also lists oil cooler hose flange screws 210 Nm and sight glass retaining screws 22 Nm if disturbed.
- Isolation / safety: PTW required; minimum two technicians; no lone working in nacelle. Do not start if 10-minute mean wind speed exceeds 15 m/s. Before opening the oil circuit, isolate per SOP-LOTO-001: inform control room and set maintenance mode S310; stop turbine and wait for rotor speed below 1 rpm; engage rotor lock pins; open main circuit breaker and UPS output breaker and apply padlocks/tags; release pitch/yaw brake accumulator pressure to 0 bar; use group lock box if more than two people; verify by local start attempt, absence of voltage at converter, and 0 bar on gauges. Drain oil only at 40–60 °C and use hot-oil PPE.
- Key execution steps: take used-oil sample; drain approx. 410 L from sump and cooling/filter circuit; inspect/clean magnetic plug; replace filter; refit drain plug; flush with 60 L PWG 220 and run electric oil pump 30 min, then drain flush oil; fill 410 L PWG 220 through 10 micron filter cart; run electric oil pump 15 min and leak-check; after 20 min standstill check sight glass and top up with PWG 220 only; check controller parameter GBX_TMIN_START = 5 °C and label filler “PWG 220”; restart after lockout removal and monitor oil temperature for first hour; take reference oil sample after 24 h operation; record quantities and batch numbers and send completion form to Litware within 30 days.
- Conflict note: the OEM Rev. D excerpt still lists PWG 320 as the approved lubricant, but it also says chapter changes are published as service bulletins. The current site SOP Rev. B is later and states it implements MOC-2025-012 and SB-LWS-2025-07 Rev. A changing the oil to PWG 220; use Rev. B for this work pack and do not top up a converted gearbox with PWG 320.

questions.question: Use the audit-readiness skill to prepare the regulator's review of the bat protection curtailment: which permit conditions apply and what evidence exists?

answer.text:
Audit-readiness summary for the regulator’s review of bat protection curtailment:

Applicable permit conditions:
- Current permit source: consolidated EP-2018-0417, incorporating variation 2 dated 2024-12-10 for bat protection curtailment, condition 7.3.
- 7.1: Bat activity must be monitored at the nacelle of WTG-04 with an acoustic detector from April to October each year.
- 7.2: Monitoring results must be reported in the annual environmental report.
- 7.3: From 1 June to 31 August each year, WTG-03, WTG-04 and WTG-05 must be stopped between 22:00 and 05:00 local time whenever hub-height wind speed is below 6.0 m/s and air temperature is 10 °C or higher.
- 7.4: Curtailment must be implemented automatically by the turbine control system, and each curtailment period must be recorded in the turbine event log.
- 7.5: Curtailment records must be kept for 5 years and summarised in an annual report submitted to the Authority by 31 January of the following year.
- 7.6: The Authority may adjust the condition 7.3 thresholds after three years of monitoring data.

Evidence found:
- The current permit identifies the reason for variation 2: Skelvane Wood, east of WTG-03 to WTG-05, holds a protected bat maternity roost and bats forage near the turbines on warm, calm summer nights.
- The site layout marks Skelvane Wood as the bat roost and WTG-03 to WTG-05 as the environmental permit curtailment group.
- The 2026-06-18 O&M minutes state that the bat protection curtailment season started on 1 June for WTG-03, WTG-04 and WTG-05 under permit condition 7.3, and that Yusuf Arkwell checked the curtailment settings in the turbine controllers on 2026-05-28.
- The 2026-07-15 handover says WTG-03, WTG-04 and WTG-05 would stop from 22:00 if wind stayed low, describes this as bat curtailment, and instructs staff not to reset it.
- The 2026-07-29 handover again records that night bat curtailment was expected for WTG-03, WTG-04 and WTG-05 in low wind.
- Site induction material supports operational awareness: some turbines stop automatically for permit reasons and such stops must never be overridden.

Evidence gaps for regulator readiness:
- No turbine event logs showing each actual curtailment period were provided.
- No annual environmental report or annual curtailment summary submitted to the Authority was provided.
- No acoustic detector monitoring results for WTG-04 were provided.
- No evidence was provided on whether the 7.3 wind-speed and temperature thresholds have been reviewed or adjusted after three years of monitoring data.
